questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can temporarily blind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign. It tells drivers that a curve is coming up on the road.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. This helps you stay in your lane, maintain control, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the side of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both driving on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both driving on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Traffic in both directions must stop. Stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is no longer extended.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You notice a defect that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well, oncoming lights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block the vehicle.
Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to clear the way for the emergency vehicle. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Make a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. Change lanes if you can, so you do not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. Change lanes if you can, so you do not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes if possible to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and stay as far away as possible. Always slow down when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to protect yourself in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations before they happen and take action to stop accidents. It helps you avoid crashes caused by other drivers who are aggressive, careless, or unsafe.

questions.question: Which must you obey first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions are more important than signs, signals, or road markings. Police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no car in either lane may cross them. You can only cross them to turn into a driveway or business entrance. Passing is never allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When entering heavy traffic on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Cars on the interstate must wave you into traffic.
You must let the cars already on the interstate go first.
You do not need to use your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let the cars already on the interstate go first.
questions.explanation: When you merge onto an interstate, you must yield to cars already on it. Always use your signal when merging.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that you will see two-way traffic ahead.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must other drivers plan for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller cars. Stay where the truck driver can see you, and make sure the truck does not block your view of traffic.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a line through it on a sign mean?

options.text: Drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not do this action.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means you cannot do that action. These signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and red and black markings.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle past you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop right away. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other cars?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with the traffic and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to tell drivers you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, there is more chance of a crash. If you drive faster than others, you have to keep passing. Drive at the same speed as traffic, within the legal limit, and pass only when you need to.
